$comment: Tools the brains may call. Each is an HTTP endpoint on the tool API (Tools:BaseUrl) described for the brains. functionName is what LLM brains see; tool/action identify it in logs. parameters: type url | text. confirmation is shown when the tool is chosen ({name} is replaced by the parameter; confirmationWithoutOptional is used when an optional parameter is missing). http.path is relative to Tools:BaseUrl, with {name} replaced by the URL-encoded parameter. classification: Internal | External (where the tool runs). outputLabel: Public | Engagement | CustomerConfidential | Secret (how sensitive its results are). outputTrust: Trusted | Untrusted (tool output that a scanned target can influence is Untrusted). requiresScope: the url parameter must be inside the session's approved engagement scope. keywords: words the rule-based keyword brain matches for tools it has no special handling for. Agents are defined in agents.json and appear here as tools automatically.

tools.description: Scan a website URL and return the links found on it (link text and URL). Use for requests to scan, crawl, map, or list/enumerate the links on a site.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The target URL or domain, e.g. https://example.com or example.com.

tools.confirmation: I'll scan {url} for links using the SimpleScanner tool.

tools.description: Run a simulated attack against a website URL and report the outcome. Use only when the user explicitly asks to attack, exploit, hack or breach a site.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The target URL or domain, e.g. https://example.com or example.com.

tools.confirmation: This looks like an attack request. I'll run a simulated attack against {url} once you approve.

tools.description: Get a five-day weather forecast (temperatures and a summary per day). Use for questions about the weather, forecast or temperature.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The place the user asked about, e.g. London. Omit it if the user didn't name one.

tools.confirmation: I'll get the weather forecast for {location}.
